Thanks Marissa — appreciated. Quick follow-up from the product side after syncing with the stakeholders: we need to expand the trial to include an entity extraction/classification use case (incoming support messages) in addition to the search scenario. Two asks: 

1) Can Redwood add a lightweight extraction endpoint (NER + intent classification) to the POC scope? Accuracy on extraction is primary for that use case (target F1 >= 0.82). Latency can be slightly higher (p95 < 500ms).
2) Given the added use case, can we rebaseline timelines? We may need the trial extended by one week to complete labeling and evaluation.

We attached a short PDF with the updated requirements and example support messages. Let us know whether this changes anything on your side.

—David

Appreciate the clarification, David — adding the extraction/classification use case is doable but has some implications. Quick internal notes and questions for ACME so we can rebaseline properly: 

- Tech impact (to confirm with engineering): add a second endpoint with NER+intent models; may require extra labeling for high-quality F1 assessment.
- Metrics to update: add F1 >= 0.82 for extraction; keep relevance NDCG target but we should specify labeling method (binary judgments vs graded).
- Timeline: propose extending trial by 1 week (new end date +7 days) to allow labeling + evaluation.
- Data handoff: ACME to provide ~1k labeled support messages or labeling plan.
- Ownership: ACME provides labels (Samantha), Redwood to produce evaluation harness + baseline run (Vivek & Monica).

Rishi — can you confirm sales-side approvals on the timeline shift and whether we need a contract addendum for the week extension? Vivek/Monica — can you review feasibility and any infra/cost implications?

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap + proposed success criteria

Looping in technical details — short answers: yes we can add the extraction endpoint. Notes: 

- Infra: adding the second endpoint increases reserved tokens and throughput needs; estimate +15% GPU usage during peak eval runs. No infra blockers for a one-week extension.
- Evaluation: to hit F1 0.82 we should get at least 1,000 labeled examples (Samantha's note) with a balanced class distribution. If ACME can only provide unlabeled data, we can run an initial zero-shot and then suggest a small labeling batch (~300 examples) for calibration — that will lower confidence in meeting the F1 target.
- Latency: p95 < 500ms is achievable if we prioritize a quantized model variant for the extraction endpoint. That will slightly affect recall; we should include both quantized and fp16 runs in the eval.
- Costs: expect ~10-18% incremental cost for the extended runs depending on batching. I'll prepare a short MOP update and cost note.

Action items for engineering: Vivek to deliver eval harness changes by Fri 2/20 EOD; need sample data by Wed 2/18 to keep timeline.

—Vivek
